lesson.title: Introduce your professional role
lesson.objective: Introduce your professional role in Spanish, name the services you handle and ask what a new client needs.
lesson.focus: Ser for profession and identity, first-person work verbs, and usted with a new client.

Refers to the whole system of recording money. Use llevar la contabilidad for keeping the books.
Use for the person or business that hires you. Its plural is clientes and it does not change for gender.

A paper or digital record. Plural documentos.
Plural in ordinary speech. The specific tax (renta, IVA) depends on the jurisdiction.
A fixed time to meet. Pedir cita means to request an appointment.
A financial institution where a business keeps its accounts.
A piece of work a professional provides for a fee.
A firm that handles accounts, payroll and tax filings for businesses. Common in Spain and some Latin American countries.

words.es: Soy contadora y trabajo con pequeños negocios.
words.en: I am an accountant and I work with small businesses.

words.note: Me encargo de means I take responsibility for a task.
Fixed polite formula with usted. ¿En qué puedo ayudarlo? or ayudarla is also correct.

words.en: Do you also review the taxes?

lesson.speaking: Introduce yourself to a new bakery owner in Spanish. Name two services you provide, then ask what the owner needs most this month. Close by agreeing on one next step.
lesson.partnerRole: Bakery owner meeting the bookkeeper for the first time, speaking Spanish with a polite tone.
lesson.openingLine: Buenos días, ¿usted es la contadora que nos recomendaron?

grammar.focus: Use ser to say who someone is: identity, profession or category (Soy contadora). Use estar for location and current states (Estoy en la oficina). With a new client use usted, which takes the third-person verb: usted trabaja, usted revisa.

examples.es: Soy contadora y trabajo con pequeños negocios.
examples.en: I am an accountant and I work with small businesses.

examples.es: Ahora estoy en la oficina del cliente.
examples.en: Right now I am at the client's office.

passage.title: Primera visita a la oficina

Elena: Sí, preparo las declaraciones y reviso cada documento del mes.

Today she receives a new client, Ramón Ortiz, who owns a bakery.

example.target: Ayudo a mis clientes con los impuestos.
example.native: I help my clients with their taxes.

verbs.note: Ayudar takes a direct object: la ayudo, lo ayudo, los ayudo. Le ayudo is also heard, especially with usted. Con introduces the task.

example.target: Preparo las declaraciones de cada mes.
example.native: I prepare the returns each month.

verbs.note: Regular -ar pattern. Preparar takes a direct object (las declaraciones), so no preposition is needed.

example.target: Reviso los documentos antes de firmar.
example.native: I review the documents before signing.

verbs.note: Antes de plus an infinitive means before doing something: antes de firmar means before signing. The infinitive does not change.

lesson.title: Arrange a client meeting
lesson.objective: Confirm a client appointment in Spanish, including time, format and the documents the client must bring.
lesson.focus: Formal commands with usted and indirect object pronouns with confirmar and enviar.

words.note: A planned conversation between people for a purpose. Often used for any scheduled meeting.
A fixed time for a meeting. Often used with a professional or medical service.
A call over the internet with video. Common across Spanish-speaking countries.
Often shortened to correo or mail in conversation. Both are common.
Also means direction. Context shows the meaning.
A proof of payment for a purchase. Some regions also use it for a utility bill.
The regular account summary from a bank. Spain and some countries also say extracto de cuenta.
A paper or digital record a client must send or keep.
The place where a business works.
Confirmar una cita, un pago o un dato: to check and state that it is correct. It takes a direct object.

words.es: Le confirmo la cita del martes.
words.en: I am confirming your Tuesday appointment.
words.note: Use le for a client. Confirmar is often followed by the object: la cita, el pago, la reunión.

words.en: Can we hold the meeting by video call?

words.es: Envíe los documentos al correo de la oficina.
words.en: Send the documents to the office email.
words.note: Usted command. Regular -ar verbs end in -e: envíe; the accent on the i stays.

words.es: Traiga los recibos y el extracto bancario.
words.en: Bring the receipts and the bank statement.
words.note: Usted command of traer, for a meeting in person.
Le viene bien is a common polite phrase for convenience.

lesson.speaking: Call a client to confirm a Tuesday meeting. Give the time, offer an in-person or video option, and list two documents to bring. End by asking the client to repeat the time and confirm.
lesson.partnerRole: Small business client who needs to confirm a meeting and the documents for it.
lesson.openingLine: Hola, llamo para confirmar la reunión del martes con la contadora.

grammar.focus: Use the usted command form (traiga, envíe) for polite instructions to a client, and use necesitar plus an infinitive to state your own need. The command form uses the same stem as the present subjunctive, so traer becomes traiga and enviar becomes envíe.

examples.es: Por favor, traiga los recibos y el extracto bancario.
examples.en: Please bring the receipts and the bank statement.

examples.es: Necesito traer los recibos de la panadería.
examples.en: I need to bring the bakery receipts.

Asistente: Le confirmo la cita del martes a las diez de la mañana con la contadora.
Ramón: ¿Podemos hacer la reunión por videollamada en vez de ir a la oficina?
Asistente: Sí. En ese caso, envíe los documentos al correo de la oficina antes del lunes.
Ramón: De acuerdo. ¿Qué documentos necesita la contadora?
Asistente: Los recibos de marzo y el extracto bancario de este mes.
Asistente: ¿Su correo electrónico y su dirección siguen siendo los de su última factura?
Ramón: El correo, sí; la dirección cambió y ahora es calle Mayor 12.
Asistente: Perfecto, actualizo sus datos, le envío el enlace y nos vemos el martes a las diez.
native: Elena's assistant calls Ramón to confirm Tuesday's meeting.
Assistant: I am confirming your Tuesday appointment with the accountant at ten in the morning.
Ramón: Can we hold the meeting by video call instead of going to the office?
Assistant: Yes. In that case, send the documents to the office email before Monday.
Ramón: All right. Which documents does the accountant need?
Assistant: The March receipts and this month's bank statement.
Assistant: Are your email and your address still the ones on your last invoice?
Ramón: The email, yes; the address changed and it is now 12 Calle Mayor.
Assistant: Perfect, I will update your details, send you the link, and we will meet on Tuesday at ten.

example.target: Traigo los recibos a la reunión.
example.native: I bring the receipts to the meeting.

example.target: Envío la confirmación hoy mismo.
example.native: I will send the confirmation today.

verbs.note: The accent on envío, envías, envía and envían marks the stressed i. Enviamos has no accent because the stress falls on the e.

example.target: Llamo al cliente para confirmar.
example.native: I call the client to confirm.

verbs.note: A regular -ar verb. Llamar a means to call a person; llamar para means to call in order to.

lesson.title: Identify a financial document
lesson.objective: Identify four common financial documents in Spanish and explain how each one differs.
lesson.focus: Demonstratives este, esta, estos and estas with ser for singular and plural identification.

words.note: The periodic summary from a bank or credit provider. The Spanish phrase estado de cuenta is widely used.
A bill that a seller issues to a buyer for goods or services. It states who sold, who bought, and the amount due.
A proof that money was paid. A receipt is not the same as an invoice.
A general term for a voucher or proof. In some countries it is used for a tax receipt or a payment slip.
A form that reports income or activity to a tax authority. The exact form depends on the jurisdiction.
A business that sells goods or services to your client. Plural proveedores.
A duplicate of an original document. Originals and copies are often filed separately.
The first version of a document, which may be needed for certification.
The date printed on a document. Check it before recording.
The final amount. Use total pagado for the amount paid.

words.es: Este documento es un estado de cuenta.
words.en: This document is a bank statement.

words.es: ¿Este papel es un recibo o una factura?
words.en: Is this paper a receipt or an invoice?
It is a receipt from the supplier.

words.es: Guardo las copias de los documentos.
words.en: I keep copies of the documents.
words.note: Guardo means I keep or store. Use with copias de when filing.

lesson.speaking: Hold up a bank statement and a receipt. Ask a coworker which is which, explain the difference in one sentence each, and agree where each document will be filed.
lesson.partnerRole: Coworker sorting documents in a small accounting office.
lesson.openingLine: Tenemos una pila de papeles. ¿Este documento es una factura o un recibo?

grammar.focus: Este and esta agree with the noun in gender and number: este documento, esta factura, estos documentos, estas facturas. Use es for one document and son for two or more; ser marks identity or category, so es un recibo names what the document is.

examples.es: Este documento es un estado de cuenta.
examples.en: This document is a bank statement.

examples.es: Estos documentos son facturas de proveedores.
examples.en: These documents are supplier invoices.

Clara: These invoices are for the bakery purchases, right?

Clara: Then I keep copies of the documents and set aside last year's tax return.

words.en: I keep copies of the documents.

example.target: Identifico cada documento por su fecha.
example.native: I identify each document by its date.

verbs.note: A regular -ar verb with no spelling change in the yo form (identifico). Identificar takes a direct object and often pairs with por when naming a method.

example.target: Guardo las facturas en la carpeta.
example.native: I keep the invoices in the folder.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb with a direct object. Guardar means to store or keep something physically or digitally.

example.target: Separo los recibos por mes.
example.native: I sort the receipts by month.

verbs.note: Regular -ar. It takes a direct object and often pairs with por to show how items are grouped.

example.target: ¿Revisa usted el extracto con el recibo?
example.native: Do you check the statement against the receipt?

verbs.note: Revisa is the form for él, ella and usted. Revisar A con B means to check A against B.

lesson.title: Read amounts and currencies
lesson.objective: Read a monetary amount in Spanish, name its currency and repeat it back before recording it.
lesson.focus: Spanish number formats (decimal comma, point thousands separator) and the currency noun after the figure.

words.note: The sum of money in a transaction. Use in formal records and bank communications.
The money a transaction uses. Check it before recording any figure.
A number that represents an amount. Often used for a total or a balance.
The hundredth of a euro. In Latin America the word is centavo.
The gap between two numbers. Use for mismatched totals.
Money placed into an account. A deposit can also be a fee or security amount in some contexts.
A short name for the bank statement. Context makes it clear.
A written or digital entry. Use registrar to record a transaction.
The final sum of several amounts.
A bank account or a ledger account. Context shows which.

words.es: Confirmo que la moneda es euro.
words.en: I confirm that the currency is euro.
I repeat the figure on the receipt.

words.es: Anoto la diferencia en el registro.
words.en: I record the difference in the record.
words.note: Anotar means to write down or note; use it for short records.

lesson.speaking: Read an amount from a receipt to a coworker in Spanish, including the currency and the cents. Ask the coworker to repeat it, and agree the figure before you record it.
lesson.partnerRole: Coworker checking a payment amount before entering it in the ledger.
lesson.openingLine: ¿Qué monto dice el recibo? Quiero confirmarlo antes de registrarlo.

grammar.focus: Spain and many South American countries write a decimal comma and a point for thousands: 1.250,50 euros. Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean usually write 1,250.50. Put the currency after the figure and say céntimos (euro) or centavos.

examples.es: El monto es 1.250,50 euros.
examples.en: The amount is 1,250.50 euros.

examples.es: Repito la cifra: mil doscientos cincuenta euros con cincuenta céntimos.
examples.en: I repeat the figure: one thousand two hundred fifty euros and fifty cents.

Julián: No, el extracto dice 1.205,50 euros en la misma fecha.
Marta: Repito la cifra del recibo: mil doscientos cincuenta euros con cincuenta céntimos.
Julián: Confirmo que la moneda es euro, no dólar, y que la cifra no coincide.
Marta: Anoto la diferencia de 45,00 euros en el registro.
Julián: Sumo el total otra vez y lo comparo con el extracto.
native: Marta and Julián review a deposit that reached the business account.
Marta: The amount is 1,250.50 euros, correct?
Julián: No, the statement says 1,205.50 euros on the same date.
Marta: I repeat the figure from the receipt: one thousand two hundred fifty euros and fifty cents.
Julián: I confirm that the currency is euro, not dollar, and that the figure does not match.
Marta: I note the 45.00-euro difference in the log.
Julián: I add the total again and compare it with the statement.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Use sumar a for adding something to a total.

example.target: Repito el monto para confirmarlo.
example.native: I repeat the amount to confirm it.

verbs.note: Stem vowel change e to i in the yo, tú, él and ellos forms (repito, repites, repiten). Nosotros keeps the e: repetimos.

example.target: Anoto el monto en el registro.
example.native: I note the amount in the record.

verbs.note: Regular -ar. Anotar is for short written notes; registrar is for official entries.

example.target: Registramos el depósito hoy.
example.native: We record the deposit today.

verbs.note: Regular -ar. The yo form registro is also the noun registro, a record or log.

lesson.title: Confirm dates and periods
lesson.objective: Ask which month, quarter or tax year a document covers and state the period in Spanish.
lesson.focus: Prepositions de, a, desde and hasta in date periods, and day-month-year order.

words.note: A span of time for a report. Período, with an accent, is also correct. Plural periodos.
A three-month period. Q1 is the first trimestre.
The twelve-month period a government or company uses for taxes and reporting. The months depend on the jurisdiction.
The day a transaction or document is dated. Use fecha de vencimiento for a due date.
The day a payment or filing must be made. Common in banking and tax notices.
A short report of results over a period.
A time limit for a task. Plazo is often used with a filing or payment.
Bank or account summary for a period.
A record or paper that shows information.
A calendar month. Plural meses.

words.en: Which period does this document cover?

words.es: Cubre desde el 1 de enero hasta el 31 de marzo.
words.en: It covers from 1 January to 31 March.

words.es: Le envío el resumen hoy mismo.
words.en: I will send you the summary today.
words.note: Spanish often uses the present for a near future action.

lesson.speaking: Ask a client which period a statement covers. Confirm the period using desde and hasta for exact days and de a for months, then state the due date and close by agreeing the next step.
lesson.partnerRole: Client who wants to know which period a document covers before sending it.
lesson.openingLine: ¿Qué periodo cubre este documento? Lo necesito para el informe.

grammar.focus: Use de and a for month ranges (de enero a marzo) and desde and hasta for exact dates (desde el 1 de enero hasta el 31 de marzo). Spanish writes the day first, then de, then the month, then de and the year.

examples.es: El extracto cubre de enero a marzo.
examples.en: The statement covers January to March.

examples.es: Cubre desde el 1 de enero hasta el 31 de marzo.
examples.en: It covers from 1 January to 31 March.

passage.title: Qué periodo cubre el extracto
target: Mónica pregunta qué periodo cubre el extracto que recibió el cliente.
Cliente: El documento cubre todo el año, ¿verdad?
Mónica: No, cubre desde el 1 de enero hasta el 31 de marzo de 2026, es decir, de enero a marzo.
Cliente: Entonces es solo el primer trimestre, no todo el año fiscal.
Mónica: Así es, y le envío hoy mismo el resumen del primer trimestre de 2026.
Cliente: ¿Cuál es la fecha de vencimiento para enviarle el resto?
Mónica: Nuestro plazo interno cierra el 10 de abril, así que conviene enviarlo esta semana.
native: Mónica asks which period the statement that the client received covers.
Client: The document covers the whole year, right?
Mónica: No, it covers from 1 January to 31 March 2026, that is, January to March.
Client: So it is only the first quarter, not the whole fiscal year.
Mónica: That's right, and I will send you the summary of the first quarter of 2026 today.
Client: What is the due date for sending you the rest?
Mónica: Our internal deadline closes on 10 April, so it is best to send it this week.

example.target: La oficina cierra el trimestre el 10 de abril.
example.native: The office closes the quarter on 10 April.

verbs.note: Stem vowel change e to ie in the present (cierro). The nosotros form keeps the e: cerramos.

example.target: El extracto indica la fecha de corte.
example.native: The statement indicates the cut-off date.

verbs.note: Regular -ar. Indicar takes a direct object (the fecha); in a formal letter the verb is common for stating a requirement.

lesson.title: Ask about income and expenses
lesson.objective: Ask simple questions in Spanish to separate income a business earned from the costs it paid, and answer with amounts.
lesson.focus: Question words cuánto, cuántos, qué and the preterite of regular -ar verbs for completed amounts.

words.note: Money a business receives from sales or services. Plural ingresos.
Money a business pays out. Gastos is plural.
A transaction in which goods or services are sold.
A business that sells goods or services to yours.
Money paid to settle a bill or a debt.
A payment or task that is not finished yet. Pendiente is an adjective; it agrees with the noun.
Use pasado after the month to say last month. Useful in financial conversations.
What remains after expenses are subtracted from income. Not the same as cash in the bank.
The moment or act of receiving money owed to you.
A number used for an amount, a total or a balance.

words.en: How much did the bakery earn this month?
What expenses did the business pay?
words.note: Pagó is preterite of pagar, the completed action.

words.es: Ganó más de lo que gastó.
words.en: It earned more than it spent.

words.note: Queda is a common way to ask what remains.

words.es: Los ingresos suben y los gastos bajan.

lesson.speaking: Interview a bakery owner about last month. Ask how much the shop earned, which costs it paid, and whether any payment is still pending. Repeat the two totals and state which one is larger.
lesson.partnerRole: Bakery owner answering questions about last month's sales and supplier bills.
lesson.openingLine: Buenos días. ¿Qué quiere saber sobre el negocio del mes pasado?

grammar.focus: Spanish question words carry an accent: cuánto (how much), cuántos (how many), qué (what). Use the preterite for a completed amount in the past: ganó (earned) and gastó (spent) are third-person forms that refer to a finished period.

Owner: The income was 3,200 euros from market sales.
Lorena: And what expenses did the business pay?
Owner: I paid for the flour and the electricity, in total I spent 1,150 euros.
Lorena: So the profit was 2,050 euros, right?
Owner: Yes, but a café has not yet paid last week's invoice.
Lorena: I note that collection as pending, and tomorrow I will confirm it with the café.

passage.title: El saldo no es lo que puedo gastar

Mario: Exactly: the balance is not negative, but the money available is lower.
Julia: I note the book balance and the available balance separately, along with the pending charge.

lesson.title: Explain debit and credit in context

lesson.speaking: Give a short lesson to a new bookkeeper: explain which side of a ledger a debit goes on, then explain which everyday card or loan the word refers to in a bank. Ask the bookkeeper to repeat the difference back.
lesson.partnerRole: New bookkeeper who keeps confusing debe, débito and crédito.
lesson.openingLine: Me confunden las palabras debe, débito y crédito. ¿Puede explicármelas?

grammar.focus: El debe (noun) is the debit side of an entry; debe is also a form of deber (must; to owe), so debe pagar means must pay. Débito and crédito name entries in bookkeeping, but cards and loans in banking.

examples.es: En la contabilidad, el debe está a la izquierda del asiento.
examples.en: In bookkeeping, the debit side is on the left of the entry.

examples.es: La tarjeta de débito descuenta el dinero de la cuenta al instante.
examples.en: The debit card takes the money from the account immediately.

passage.title: Debe, haber y tarjetas
target: Patricia enseña a Rubén cómo leer un asiento en el libro mayor.
Patricia: El debe está a la izquierda y el haber a la derecha.
Rubén: ¿Entonces débito y crédito son lo mismo que la tarjeta de débito?
Patricia: No, en la contabilidad son columnas; la tarjeta es un medio de pago.
Rubén: Y la tarjeta de crédito, ¿es un préstamo del banco?
Patricia: En la práctica sí: el banco presta dinero hasta el límite y el titular debe devolver lo gastado.
Rubén: Entonces cada compra tiene un débito en una cuenta y un crédito en otra, aunque se pague con tarjeta.
Patricia: Exacto; una compra con tarjeta de crédito va al debe de gastos y al haber de la deuda con la tarjeta.
native: Patricia shows Rubén how to read an entry in the ledger.
Patricia: The debit side is on the left and the credit side on the right.
Rubén: So debit and credit are the same as the debit card?
Patricia: No, in bookkeeping they are columns; the card is a means of payment.
Rubén: And the credit card, is it a loan from the bank?
Patricia: In practice, yes: the bank lends money up to the limit, and the cardholder must pay back what was spent.
Rubén: So every purchase has a debit in one account and a credit in another, even when it is paid by card.
Patricia: Exactly; a credit card purchase goes on the debit side of expenses and the credit side of the card liability.

lesson.title: Read a ledger with a coworker
lesson.objective: Read a ledger with a coworker in Spanish and explain how an entry changed an account, using the imperfect for a past state and the preterite for an event.

passage.title: Una entrada en el libro mayor

lesson.title: Plan a business budget
lesson.objective: Ask in Spanish about expected revenue, recurring costs and a planned purchase for a business budget, using the future and the first conditional.

lesson.speaking: Plan next quarter's budget with a client who wants to buy a new delivery van. Ask about expected revenue and recurring costs, state two assumptions, and say what the business can afford if sales rise. Close by agreeing to review the plan at the end of the month.
lesson.partnerRole: Owner of a delivery business in Spain who wants to know whether the budget can support a van purchase.
lesson.openingLine: Quiero comprar una furgoneta para las entregas. ¿Cómo lo planeamos?

grammar.focus: The future adds endings to the infinitive: venderemos, gastaremos. A real condition uses si plus the present, then the future: si vendemos más, podremos comprar la furgoneta. Ir a plus an infinitive states a plan: vamos a revisar.

passage.title: Presupuesto para una camioneta
target: Andrea y Hugo preparan el presupuesto del próximo trimestre para el servicio de entregas.
Hugo: Quiero comprar una furgoneta; ¿cuánto esperamos vender?
Andrea: Los ingresos previstos son de 18.000 euros, según el supuesto de volumen de entregas.
Hugo: ¿Y los costos fijos y variables?
Andrea: Los fijos son 6.500 euros de alquiler y personal; los variables, unos 3.000 euros de combustible y peajes.
Andrea: Con ese escenario, el margen previsto es de unos 8.500 euros antes de la compra planificada.

Andrea: Vamos a revisar el presupuesto a fin de mes para confirmar ese escenario y el flujo de efectivo.
native: Andrea and Hugo prepare next quarter's budget for the delivery service.
Hugo: I want to buy a van; how much do we expect to sell?
Andrea: Expected revenue is 18,000 euros, based on the delivery volume assumption.
Hugo: And the fixed and variable costs?
Andrea: The fixed costs are 6,500 euros for rent and staff; the variable ones, about 3,000 euros for fuel and tolls.
Andrea: In that scenario, the expected margin is about 8,500 euros before the planned purchase.
Hugo: If we sell more than expected, we will be able to buy the van before June.
Andrea: We are going to review the budget at the end of the month to confirm that scenario and the cash flow.

passage.title: Cotización de un préstamo
target: Iván recibe una cotización de préstamo para su taller y la revisa con su asesora, Elena Ramos.
Iván: El capital es de 20.000 euros a cinco años, así que esperaba una cuota mensual de unos 333 euros, no de 387.
Elena: La cuota incluye capital e intereses; esta cotización indica un interés fijo del 6 % anual.
Iván: ¿Y la comisión de apertura? ¿Se suma a la cuota?
Elena: No, se paga una vez al inicio: son 200 euros, el 1 % del capital.
Iván: Entonces ¿cuál es el costo total del préstamo?
Elena: Tanto los intereses, unos 3.200 euros, como la comisión forman el costo: unos 3.400 euros además del capital.
Iván: Gracias. Quiero el cronograma de pagos antes de decidir.
native: Iván receives a loan quote for his workshop and reviews it with his adviser, Elena Ramos.
Iván: The principal is 20,000 euros over five years, so I expected a monthly payment of about 333 euros, not 387.
Elena: The payment includes principal and interest; this quote shows a fixed interest rate of 6% a year.
Iván: And the arrangement fee? Is it added to the payment?
Elena: No, it is paid once at the start: 200 euros, 1% of the principal.
Iván: So what is the total cost of the loan?
Elena: Both the interest, about 3,200 euros, and the fee make up the cost: about 3,400 euros on top of the principal.
Iván: Thank you. I want the payment schedule before I decide.

lesson.objective: Distinguish a tax deduction from a tax credit in Spanish on a US federal return, with fictional round figures and the comparisons más que and menos que.

An amount subtracted from the tax owed. IRS Spanish materials say crédito tributario; crédito fiscal is also common.
The amount on which tax is calculated.
The percentage applied to the taxable base.
The tax amount owed after credits.
A cost the tax rules allow to be deducted. Which costs qualify depends on the jurisdiction and the taxpayer.
The authority whose rules apply.
A teaching case that does not describe a real rule.

words.en: A deduction reduces the taxable base.

words.es: Un crédito reduce el impuesto directamente.
words.en: A credit reduces the tax directly.

words.en: This is a fictional example, not a real rule.

lesson.speaking: Explain to a client in the United States, with fictional round figures, how a deduction and a credit reduce federal income tax differently. Give one example of each, state which one reduces the base and which reduces the tax itself, then check the client understands.

passage.title: Deducción y crédito en un ejemplo
target: Marta, preparadora de impuestos en Houston, explica a un cliente la diferencia entre una deducción y un crédito tributario en la declaración federal.
Cliente: ¿Son lo mismo? Los dos bajan el impuesto, ¿no?
Marta: No: una deducción reduce la base imponible, y un crédito reduce el impuesto directamente.
Cliente: ¿Cómo se ve eso con números?
Marta: En un ejemplo ficticio con una tasa impositiva del 20 %, una deducción de 1.000 dólares ahorra 200 dólares de impuesto.
Cliente: ¿Y un crédito de 1.000 dólares?
Marta: Reduce el impuesto a pagar en 1.000 dólares, así que vale más que una deducción del mismo importe.
Cliente: Entendido: con la misma cifra, la deducción vale menos que el crédito.

Hernán: La diferencia es de 300 euros. ¿No será el transporte, sumado dos veces?
Vanessa: Es posible; por eso es necesario que revisemos la fuente original de cada cifra.
Hernán: El proveedor me habló de una nota de crédito. ¿Qué documento la refleja?
Vanessa: Ninguno de los dos todavía, y no sabemos si es un pago parcial o una corrección.
Vanessa: Pido la factura original, la nota de crédito y el detalle del estado de cuenta para que confirmemos el importe antes del viernes.
Hernán: Mientras tanto, no quiero cambiar el registro.
Vanessa: Correcto, no cambiamos el registro hasta tener la prueba; esperamos la confirmación del proveedor.
Hernán: ¿Y quién decide cuál es la cifra final?
Vanessa: La decide el documento fuente, no una preferencia; el lunes le confirmo por escrito el resultado.
Hernán: Entiendo; prefiero no pagar la diferencia hasta tener esa respuesta.
Vanessa: Así evitamos pagar dos veces el mismo importe, y el registro queda limpio.

Vanessa: I am requesting the original invoice, the credit note and the statement detail so that we can confirm the amount before Friday.
Hernán: In the meantime, I do not want to change the record.

Hernán: And who decides which figure is final?

Hernán: I understand; I prefer not to pay the difference until I have that answer.

Cliente: Entonces, ¿no tengo que pagar todavía la cuota ni una sanción?

Celia: Mantenga los documentos a mano hasta que respondamos; necesitaré las facturas de 2024.

Celia: Sí, le confirmo el plazo de respuesta por escrito hoy mismo.

Client: It says proposed amount, 2,300 euros, but I do not know whether it is the final bill.
Celia: This notice is not the final bill; it is a proposed assessment with a deadline for replying.
Client: What kind of reply does it ask for?
Celia: Look at the line with the response deadline: it allows you to submit a reply with supporting documentation, and it does not ask for immediate payment.
Client: So I do not have to pay the tax amount or a penalty yet?
Celia: Not yet; if the Agency keeps the figure after our reply, the final assessment will state the payment deadline.
Celia: Keep the documents to hand until we reply; I will need the 2024 invoices.
Client: All right. Will you confirm the deadline in writing?
Celia: Yes, I will confirm the response deadline to you in writing today.
Client: And if I do not understand a word in the notice?
Celia: Write it down, and we will review it together before replying.
Client: So, to repeat: I do not pay now, I gather the invoices, and we reply before the deadline.

Dueña: Entonces, ¿cuál recomienda usted?

Anabel: Suele ser de varios días hábiles; le confirmo la fecha exacta cuando el banco responda.

Gustavo: La orden decía gastos compartidos. ¿Qué significa eso?

Gustavo: Entonces hay dos causas posibles: el tipo de cambio y un intermediario.

Teresa: That sender fee came out of your account, so it did not reduce the amount received.
Gustavo: So did the bank keep part of the money?
Teresa: We do not know yet; an intermediary bank may have charged a fee along the way.
Gustavo: And does the currency conversion also play a part?
Teresa: Yes; the supplier received pesos, and the exchange rate applied may differ from the one he used on his invoice.
Gustavo: The order said shared charges. What does that mean?
Teresa: That you pay your own bank's fee, but other banks' fees may be deducted from the amount.
Gustavo: So there are two possible causes: the exchange rate and an intermediary.
Teresa: Exactly, and to separate them we need the transfer confirmation and the supplier's credit advice, with the amount received.

passage.title: Aprender la revisión de pagos
target: Gabriel, contador experimentado, enseña el proceso de revisión de pagos a Sofía, su nueva compañera.
Sofía: Quiero aprender bien el proceso de revisión. ¿Por dónde empiezo?
Gabriel: Primero revisa la factura, luego compara el importe con el justificante.
Sofía: ¿Y después? ¿Puedo aprobar el pago ya?
Gabriel: Todavía no; después revisa la referencia, que conecta el pago con la factura, y al final viene la aprobación.
Gabriel: ¿Me lo repites con tus palabras, para ver si está claro?
Sofía: Primero la factura, luego el importe con el justificante y al final la aprobación.
Gabriel: Casi; falta un paso. Te pido que revises la referencia antes de aprobar.
Gabriel: Ayer se omitió en un pago de otro equipo y tuvimos que corregirlo.
Sofía: ¿Un control omitido? No quiero cometer ese error.
Gabriel: Es normal al principio; por eso lo repasamos juntos ahora.
Sofía: Entonces: factura, importe con el justificante, referencia y aprobación.
Gabriel: Exacto. Anótalo en la lista de verificación con esa secuencia.
Sofía: Lo anoto, y revisamos el archivo de pago paso a paso.
Gabriel: Perfecto, y mañana vemos la revisión final del cierre.
native: Gabriel, an experienced accountant, teaches the payment review process to Sofía, his new colleague.
Sofía: I want to learn the review process properly. Where do I start?
Gabriel: First check the invoice, then compare the amount with the supporting document.
Sofía: And after that? Can I approve the payment then?
Gabriel: Not yet; next check the reference, which links the payment to the invoice, and the approval comes last.
Gabriel: Can you repeat it back in your own words, so we can see whether it is clear?
Sofía: First the invoice, then the amount against the supporting document, and finally the approval.
Gabriel: Almost; one step is missing. I would ask you to check the reference before approving.
Gabriel: Yesterday it was skipped on another team's payment, and we had to correct it.
Sofía: A skipped check? I do not want to make that mistake.
Gabriel: It is normal at the start; that is why we are going over it together now.
Sofía: So: invoice, amount against the supporting document, reference, and approval.
Gabriel: Exactly. Write it on the checklist in that sequence.
Sofía: I will write it down, and we will review the payment file step by step.
Gabriel: Perfect, and tomorrow we will look at the final review for the close.

passage.title: Cierre del caso completo
target: Carmen, contadora en Valladolid, cierra un caso complejo con su cliente, el señor Benítez, y su compañero Ulises.
Benítez: Tenemos dos registros que no coinciden y una estimación que cambió. ¿Cómo lo cerramos hoy?
Carmen: Empecemos por los registros conflictivos: su libro de ventas dice 5.800 euros cobrados, y el banco muestra 5.300.
Ulises: Hemos conciliado casi todos los registros; la diferencia de 500 euros es la única partida abierta.
Ulises: No creo que el segundo registro sea un error del banco; parece un descuento que aplicó su cliente.
Carmen: Por eso le pedimos que envíe la fuente original: la nota de crédito o el correo de su cliente.
Benítez: ¿Y eso cambia la estimación? Ya pagué el trimestre en abril.
Carmen: El pago de abril cubrió el primer trimestre; este cobro llegó en mayo y entra en el segundo.
Carmen: Con esta venta, la estimación actualizada del segundo trimestre sube, y el impacto fiscal depende de si la cifra final es 5.800 o 5.300.
Carmen: Podríamos actualizar la estimación hoy con 5.300 y corregirla si la fuente confirma otra cifra.
Benítez: De acuerdo. ¿Quién se encarga de la partida abierta?
Carmen: Traspasaremos el caso a Mauro mañana; él tendrá el plan de acción y la nota de traspaso.
Ulises: Yo le explico a Mauro la conciliación y le dejo la partida abierta documentada.
Carmen: El estado del caso queda claro por escrito: registros conciliados salvo 500 euros pendientes, y una estimación actualizada.
Benítez: Entonces yo envío la nota de crédito el jueves, y ustedes me confirman la cifra final.
Carmen: Exacto: el compromiso final es enviarle la confirmación por escrito el viernes, con el resumen de cierre.
native: Carmen, an accountant in Valladolid, closes a complex case with her client, Mr. Benítez, and her colleague Ulises.
Benítez: We have two records that do not match and an estimate that changed. How do we close it today?
Carmen: Let's start with the conflicting records: your sales book says 5,800 euros collected, and the bank shows 5,300.
Ulises: We have reconciled almost all the records; the 500-euro difference is the only open item.
Ulises: I do not think the second record is a bank error; it looks like a discount your customer applied.
Carmen: That is why we ask you to send the original source: the credit note or your customer's email.
Benítez: And does that change the estimate? I already paid the quarter in April.
Carmen: The April payment covered the first quarter; this payment came in in May and belongs to the second.
Carmen: With this sale, the updated estimate for the second quarter goes up, and the tax impact depends on whether the final figure is 5,800 or 5,300.
Carmen: We could update the estimate today with 5,300 and correct it if the source confirms a different figure.
Benítez: Agreed. Who is taking charge of the open item?
Carmen: We will hand the case over to Mauro tomorrow; he will have the action plan and the handoff note.
Ulises: I will walk Mauro through the reconciliation and leave him the open item documented.
Carmen: The case status is set out in writing: records reconciled except for 500 euros pending, and an updated estimate.
Benítez: So I will send the credit note on Thursday, and you will confirm the final figure to me.
Carmen: Exactly: the final commitment is to send you the written confirmation on Friday, with the closing summary.
